sources.entry: Navidrome Music Server - Modern Music Server and Streamer, compatible with Subsonic/Airsonic. (Demo, Source Code, Clients) GPL-3.0 Docker/Go

summary.one_liner: Navidrome is an open source, web-based music server and streamer that lets you listen to your music collection from any browser or mobile device.
summary.what_it_does: Navidrome scans a music library and serves it over a web interface built on Material UI, so it can be played from a browser or mobile device. It handles large collections and streams a wide range of audio formats. It reads existing metadata and supports compilations and multi-disc box sets. It monitors the library for file changes and imports new files or reloads metadata. Each user gets separate play counts, playlists and favourites. It transcodes on the fly, which can be set per user or player, and supports Opus encoding. The README says it is compatible with Subsonic, Madsonic and Airsonic clients.
use_cases: share music library with multiple users
browse music collection in a web browser
how_to_run: See instructions on the project's website (installation docs cover Docker, binaries, and building from source)
notable: Subsonic/Madsonic/Airsonic API compatibility, so existing music clients can connect
Multi-user with per-user play counts, playlists and favourites
Automatic library monitoring that imports new files and reloads metadata
Lyrics support from sidecar files and embedded tags, including TTML, LRC and SRT
Ready-to-use binaries including Raspberry Pi, plus Docker images
caveats: The master branch may be unstable or broken; the README recommends using releases
Cloud hosting partners are offered by the project, with revenue sharing mentioned in the README
Installation details are on the external project website rather than in the README
